places.name: Sudan
places.significance: Subject of the memo. The US policy community was reviewing US policy toward Sudan and its state of relations with the Sudanese government.

events.description: CIA Africa Division sends a memo to the Acting DCI with recommendations on US policy toward Sudan. The policy community was reviewing that policy, and the memo says Sudanese involvement with terrorism had not decreased.

The CIA Africa Division sends the Acting Director of Central Intelligence a memorandum of recommendations on Sudan while the policy community reviews U.S. policy toward Sudan. The memo is heavily excised, and its date is taken from the document header (the page shows only '1 DEC').

relationships.detail: The Africa Division is the CIA component that wrote the memorandum to the Acting Director of Central Intelligence.
relationships.quote: Acting Director of Central Intelligence Africa Division Recommendations Regarding Sudan

relationships.detail: The Sudanese government is the government of Sudan, the subject of the memorandum.
relationships.quote: state of relations with the Sudanese government

key_claims: The CIA Africa Division assessed in December 1996 that there was no indication Sudanese involvement with terrorism had decreased over the past year.
The memo suggests Sudan may be making 'tactical retreats' on support to terrorism, apparently to influence the policy review.
Most of the document is excised or illegible, so the chunk names no individuals and no other entities.
